name: Ulwa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Green, Thomas Michael. 1999. A Lexicographic Study of Ulwa. PhD dissertation, MIT (MIT DSpace hdl 1721.1/9351).
catalog_quote: p.43: "Light syllables (indicated by L in the discussion) have the structure [C0V]σ, while a syllable containing a long vowel and/or coda consonant—[C0VC]σ or [C0V:C0]σ—is heavy (H). The nature of the onset, or whether one is present at all, has no bearing on the weight of a syllable. ... Ulwa can be described as preferring to parse its phonological representations into iambic feet ... those of the form [LH], [LL], or [H]. Iambic feet are right-headed ... the rightmost syllable receives higher prominence." p.56: "The stress pattern of an Ulwa word depends not only on its phonological makeup, but also on its ... morphological structure. ... (49) a. All long vowels receive stress. b. One of the first three syllables receives stress. Syllable weight is crucial in determining the precise localization. c. sources.quote: p.132: 'por lo general no se transcriben apropiadamente los rasgos suprasegmentales ni la nasalidad vocálica. Hasta que se disponga de datos de mejor calidad en aspectos como estos para el sumo, no parece posible trabajar en la reconstrucción de otra cosa que vocales y consonantes.' No statement on Ulwa (ulua) stress placement anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent acento/stress: 0 hits).
